---
title: "check-pr-concerns.yml"
---

Diff-scoped, blocking check that fails a pull request changing both content and infrastructure.
Content and infrastructure go in separate PRs.
Whether a PR has exactly one concern cannot be decided mechanically,
so this checks the part that can be: a PR with at least one content file and at least one infrastructure file has two concerns.
This implements part of
[gha#1188](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1188).

Content paths by default are `chapters/**`, `**/_subfiles/**`, `**/*.qmd` and `**/*.Rmd`.
Infrastructure paths by default are `.github/**`, `tools/**`, `scripts/**`, `hooks/**`, `filters/**`, `.claude/**` and `_quarto*.yml`.
A path in both lists counts as infrastructure.
Lockfiles, `_freeze/`, `docs/` and `changelog.d/` count as neither.

Do not use it in a repository whose pages document its own infrastructure, such as gha itself:
every PR there touches both.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `content-paths` | built-in | Globs for content (`*`, `?`, `**`); replaces the defaults |
| `infra-paths` | built-in | Globs for infrastructure; replaces the defaults |
| `paths-ignore` | none | Extra paths counted as neither |
| `exempt-label` | `mixed-ok` | Label that lifts the check, read live through the API |
| `fail` | `true` | Block instead of warn |

## Scope

With no base to diff against, or when the diff cannot be computed,
the check skips with a warning instead of examining the whole tree.
The caller stub triggers on `labeled` and `unlabeled`,
so adding the exemption label re-runs the check.

## Example

See [`examples/check-pr-concerns.yml`](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/blob/main/examples/check-pr-concerns.yml).
